# Tracepoints

*Rewritten 2026-08-18 (Generated by Claude Fable 5, Anthropic) from
`fish_tracepoints/install_fish_tracepoints`, `config/fish_events.txt` and the
postprocess consumers. Payload field names are the ones in the
`TRACEPOINT_EVENT` definitions; probe sites are the anchors the installer
patches. Older numbers ("11 custom tracepoints", "31 events") in notes are
superseded by this page.*

FISH enables **36 LTTng-UST events**: 14 stock `ros2_tracing` events (init +
callback chain) and **22 FISH-custom `ros2:fish_*` events** added by patching
tracetools, rcl, rclcpp, rclcpp_action, rclpy and (when present) Isaac ROS
NITROS in an overlay workspace (`/root/trace_overlay_ws`). Two more stock
events (`ros2:rcl_publish`, `ros2:rmw_take`) are switched on only in
per-instance mode (see the end of this page).

Ingest (`postprocess/ingest_pg.py`) is event-agnostic: every event becomes one
`ros2_trace` row with a JSONB payload; all consumption listed below happens in
`postprocess/model_improved_pg.py`, `join_analysis.py`, `fish_viz_server.py`.

## How to read the tables

* **Execution path** — *init/structural* events fire once per object at
  creation and only build the graph; *runtime* events fire per callback
  dispatch / per message / per request and carry the timing.
* **`__fish_active_callback`** — a `__thread const void *` defined in the
  patched `libtracetools.so`. The patched `ros_trace_callback_start` wrapper
  sets it to the callback id and `ros_trace_callback_end` clears it, so any
  probe that runs *inside* a callback (publish, client request, receive) can
  stamp "which callback am I in" without touching application code. This is
  the mechanism behind every `*_link` event.

## 2. Action server dispatch — 4 FISH events (`rclcpp_action/src/server.cpp`)

| Event | Payload | Probe site | Path | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_action_server_init` | action_server_handle, action_name, goal_service_handle, cancel_service_handle, result_service_handle | `ServerBase::ServerBase()` after `rcl_action_server_init` (reads the rcl impl struct) | init | reserved (`detect_actions` currently works on `/_action/` entity labels) |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_action_execute_goal` | action_server_handle | first line of `execute_goal_request_received()` | runtime, per goal | reserved |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_action_execute_cancel` | action_server_handle | first line of `execute_cancel_request_received()` | runtime | reserved |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_action_execute_result` | action_server_handle | first line of `execute_result_request_received()` | runtime | reserved |

Why they exist: action servers are Waitables and bypass `ServiceBase`, so
stock tracing sees nothing of them. Since the executor Waitable wrap (§5)
they are also visible as ordinary F callbacks; the four events remain for
per-goal timing.

## 3. rclpy callback chain — 5 FISH events (Python, via ctypes bridge)

`fish_rclpy_trace.py` (created by the installer inside the rclpy package)
calls `ros_trace_fish_rclpy_*` in `libtracetools.so`; the callback id is
`id(callable)`; runtime boundaries reuse `callback_start/end` from
`rclpy/executors.py`.

| Event | Payload | Probe site | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ros2:fish_rclpy_subscription_callback_added` | subscription_handle, callback | `rclpy/subscription.py Subscription.__init__` | `identify_callbacks` (rclpy fallback chain) |
| `ros2:fish_rclpy_service_callback_added` | service_handle, callback | `rclpy/service.py` | same |
| `ros2:fish_rclpy_timer_callback_added` | timer_handle, callback | `rclpy/timer.py Timer.__init__` | same |
| `ros2:fish_rclpy_timer_init` | timer_handle, node_handle, period_ns | `rclpy/node.py Node.create_timer` (between `Timer(...)` and `callback_group.add_entity`) | tmr E vertices with period |
| `ros2:fish_rclpy_callback_register` | callback, symbol (`module.qualname`) | bridge `_register()` from the three `*_callback_added` helpers | F label; gantt symbols |

## 4. Service client RTT + atomic timer init — 3 FISH events

| Event | Payload | Probe site | Path | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_client_request_sent` | client_handle, sequence_number | rclcpp `client.hpp: Client<T>::async_send_request_impl()` after `rcl_send_request`; rclpy `client.py call_async`, `action/client.py send_goal_async` | runtime, per request, caller thread | `split_callbacks` (F with a client aspect → `::part1` + `::continuation`); runtime attribution fallback |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_client_response_received` | client_handle, sequence_number, response_type (0 future-only, 1 callback, 2 callback+request) | `client.hpp: handle_response()` (+ `callback_start/end` around the two callback variants); rclpy `executors.py _execute_client`, `action/client.py execute()` | runtime, executor thread | not yet consumed (RTT = response − request) |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_timer_init` | timer_handle, node_handle, period_ns | rclcpp `node_timers.cpp: NodeTimers::add_timer()` right after the stock link event | init | tmr E vertices with period (atomic replacement of `rcl_timer_init` + `rclcpp_timer_link_node`) |

## 5. Callback-link attribution — 4 FISH events (the FT backbone)

These give the *aspects* of a callback (what it publishes / requests /
receives) without per-message tracing: each probe stamps
`__fish_active_callback` and the wrapper de-duplicates per thread
(`fish_link_seen`, 128-entry cache), so the events fire ≈ once per
(handle, callback, thread) instead of once per message.

| Event | Payload | Probe sites | Path | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_publish_link` | publisher_handle, callback | (a) rcl `publisher.c: rcl_publish()`, `rcl_publish_serialized_message()`, `rcl_publish_loaned_message()`; (b) **rclcpp `publisher_base.cpp: PublisherBase::get_intra_process_subscription_count()`** — every intra-process-capable `Publisher<T>::publish()` calls it before deciding whether to skip `rcl_publish`, so intra-process-only publishes are attributed too (ABI-safe, lives in `librclcpp.so`, no downstream rebuild); (c) `publisher.hpp do_intra_process_*` (template, only for code built against the overlay); (d) NITROS `nitros_publisher.cpp: NitrosPublisher::publish()`. Wrapper skips NULL callback | runtime, deduped; publishing thread (rclpy publishes reach (a) with the Python cb id) | `attribute_aspects` → pub aspects on E/F; `detect_joins` (who completes a join); causal view |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_client_link` | client_handle, callback | rcl `client.c: rcl_send_request()` after the sequence-number exchange | runtime, deduped | `attribute_aspects` → cli aspects → `split_callbacks` |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_receive_link` | subscription_handle, callback | rclcpp `executor.cpp: Executor::execute_subscription()` first statement; NITROS `nitros_subscriber.cpp: subscriberCallback()` | runtime, deduped (NULL callback kept) | `attribute_aspects`: marks the sub aspect `received=True` (+ receiving cb addrs) |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_waitable_init` | waitable, node_handle, callback_group | (a) `node_waitables.cpp: NodeWaitables::add_waitable()`; (b) **`intra_process_manager.cpp: IntraProcessManager::add_subscription()`** with `(subscription.get(), nullptr, nullptr)` — the intra-process sentinel `node_handle=0x0` | init, once per Waitable | (a) → `waitable` E vertex (5th entity type: QoS event handlers, action client/server, NitrosPublisherWaitable, rosbag2 player…); (b) → names the `SubscriptionIntraProcess` Waitable of a subscription (`ipc_waitable`, `ipc_capable`, `delivery = ipc/dds/both`) — see `notes/CRITICAL_autoware_intraprocess_waitables.txt` |

**Executor Waitable wrap (branch 5).** `executor.cpp`
`if (any_exec.waitable) { any_exec.waitable->execute(any_exec.data); }` is
wrapped in `TRACEPOINT(callback_start, waitable.get(), false) … TRACEPOINT(callback_end, …)`.
Every Waitable dispatch therefore appears as an F with cb-id = the Waitable
`this` (for intra-process subscriptions the stock inner `callback_start`
nests inside it). Without this wrap the intra-process delivery path of
Autoware (and every action/QoS Waitable) is invisible.

## 6. NITROS GXF topology — 2 FISH events (Isaac ROS only)

| Event | Payload | Probe site | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ros2:fish_nitros_sub_link` | node_handle, group_addr, subscription_handle, entity_name, component_name | `nitros_node.cpp: postNegotiationCallback` (added getters `getCompatibleSubscriber()`) | `add_horizontal_edges` NITROS block: ingress sub of a pub/sub group |
| `ros2:fish_nitros_pub_link` | node_handle, group_addr, publisher_handle, waitable_handle, entity_name, component_name | same block (`getCompatiblePublisher()`, `getNitrosWaitable()`) | egress Waitable; ingress→egress intra-node L2/L3 edges (GXF graph inside a node) |

## 7. Scheduler introspection — 4 FISH events

| Event | Payload | Probe site | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_executor_init` | executor_addr, executor_type ("SingleThreaded" / "MultiThreaded" / "StaticSingleThreaded"), num_threads | the three executor ctors in `rclcpp/src/rclcpp/executors/`; rclpy `executors.py` executor `__init__` | `attach_callback_groups`: EX type / thread count |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_callback_group_init` | group_addr, group_type (MutuallyExclusive / Reentrant), automatic_add | `callback_group.cpp: CallbackGroup::CallbackGroup()`; rclpy `callback_groups.py` | callback-group attributes |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_cbgroup_add` | group_addr, entity_addr (rcl handle; Waitable ptr for `wait`), entity_kind (sub/tmr/srv/cli/wait) | `CallbackGroup::add_{subscription,timer,service,client,waitable}()`; rclpy `add_entity` | E/F ↔ callback group |
| `ros2:fish_rclcpp_executor_add_cbgroup` | executor_addr, group_addr, node_addr | `executor.cpp: Executor::add_callback_group_to_map()`; rclpy `Executor.add_node` | EX ↔ callback groups (which executor runs which callbacks — verified from the trace, never inferred from process count) |

## Patch mechanics (what the installer edits)

| Component | Files / anchors | What is inserted |
|---|---|---|
| tracetools (overlay, 4.1.2) | `tp_call.h` (before the final `#endif`), `tracetools.h` (before the C++ guard end), `tracetools.c` (before `pragma GCC diagnostic pop`), `tracetools_trace/tools/names.py` | 22 `TRACEPOINT_EVENT` blocks + declarations + `TRACEPOINT()` bodies; the `__fish_active_callback` thread-local and its set/clear in the `callback_start/end` wrappers; per-thread dedup caches for the `*_link` events; `DEFAULT_EVENTS_ROS` regenerated |
| rcl (overlay, 5.3.12) | `publisher.c` (after stock `rcl_publish` TP; before `rmw_publish_serialized_message`, `rmw_publish_loaned_message`), `client.c` (after the sequence-number exchange) | `publish_link`, `client_link` |
| rclcpp (overlay, 16.0.19) | `client.hpp`, `node_timers.cpp`, `callback_group.cpp`, `executor.cpp` (add_cbgroup, receive_link, **Waitable wrap**), `executors/*_executor.cpp`, `node_waitables.cpp`, `intra_process_manager.cpp`, `publisher_base.cpp`, `publisher.hpp`, `generic_subscription.hpp` | events of §4, §5, §7 and the branch-5 wrap; `generic_subscription.hpp` gets the three stock init/register events so `ros2 bag`, `ros2 topic echo`, ros2_benchmark MonitorNode and NITROS compat subs are attributable |
| rclcpp_action (overlay) | `CMakeLists.txt` (tracetools dep), `server.cpp` | §2 events |
| rclpy (patched in place, `/opt/ros/humble/…/rclpy`) | `fish_rclpy_trace.py` (new bridge), `subscription.py`, `service.py`, `timer.py`, `node.py`, `executors.py`, `callback_groups.py`, `client.py`, `action/client.py` | §3, client events, scheduler events, `callback_start/end` around Python callbacks |
| isaac_ros_nitros (only if `/root/ros_ws/src/isaac_ros_nitros` exists) | `nitros_publisher.cpp`, `nitros_subscriber.cpp`, `nitros_{publisher,subscriber}.hpp` (getters), `nitros_node.cpp`, `package.xml` | §5 (d), §6; then `colcon build --packages-select isaac_ros_nitros` |

Installer flags: `--action`, `--rclpy`, `--client`, `--link`, `--scheduler`,
`--all` (default). Images that already contain the overlay are never
modified in place — a new build produces a new image tag (fishwait3/4/5
lineage, see `images.md`).

## Dropped vanilla events and per-instance mode

14 stock events are deliberately **not** enabled (commented at the bottom of
`config/fish_events.txt`): `rcl_init`, `rmw_publisher_init`,
`rmw_subscription_init` (init-only, no consumer); `rclcpp_publish`,
`rcl_publish`, `rmw_publish`, `rmw_take`, `rcl_take`, `rclcpp_take`
(per-message — they dominate a ~36 M-event Autoware trace);
`rcl_lifecycle_*` (no consumer); `rclcpp_executor_get_next_ready`,
`rclcpp_executor_wait_for_work`, `rclcpp_executor_execute` (per spin). The
deduped `*_link` events carry the structural information instead.

`[trace] per_instance = true` (`config/fish_settings.ini`) re-enables exactly
two of them, `ros2:rcl_publish` (publisher_handle, message) and
`ros2:rmw_take` (rmw_subscription_handle, message, source_timestamp, taken),
through the generated `trace_session.sh`, which then drives `lttng` directly
(`fish_ch` channel 4 × 2 MB per CPU, needs `--shm-size ≥ 1g`; falls back to
512 K × 4; discards are reported in `fishlog/discards.txt`). They enable:

* `measure_flows` — per-instance hop latency publish→take paired by the DDS
  `source_timestamp` (same host = same clock; agreement 3–8 µs), or intra-
  process pairing when there is no take;
* `join_analysis` — completer distribution and execution time by role;
* `detect_polled_subs` — an `rmw_take` inside another callback's window is
  a *polled* (sample-and-hold) read: consumer = enclosing callback, data age
  = take − source_timestamp (`flow_method='polled_take'`).

Cost: ~+50 % events on Autoware (r11: 4.9 M vs ~3 M events for 60 s of bag).

## Event count summary

| Group | Stock | FISH custom | Consumed today |
|---|---|---|---|
| Core init + callback chain | 14 | – | 12 |
| Action server dispatch | – | 4 | 0 (reserved) |
| rclpy callback chain | – | 5 | 5 |
| Service client + atomic timer | – | 3 | 2 |
| Callback-link attribution | – | 4 | 4 |
| NITROS GXF topology | – | 2 | 2 |
| Scheduler introspection | – | 4 | 4 |
| **Whitelisted total** | **14** | **22** | 29 / 36 |
| per-instance extras | 2 (`rcl_publish`, `rmw_take`) | – | 2 |

Known caveats: rclpy `action/client.py` reports `id(self._client_handle)`
(a Python id, not the rcl handle) as `client_handle`; the per-thread 128-entry
link dedup cache stops recording new (handle, callback) pairs on a thread once
full; `notes/tracepoint_inventory.txt` (April) is stale.
